-## Selecting affected tasks instead of projects

-By default Nx selects whole projects, so every task of every affected project runs. Set `NX_LEGACY_AFFECTED=false` to select individual tasks instead, based on whether your change reaches what each task reads:

+Nx selects individual tasks, based on whether your change reaches what each task reads. Changing one spec file runs that project's `test` task rather than the `test` task of every project that depends on it. Tasks that read most of a project, like `lint`, narrow very little.

-Changing one spec file then runs that project's `test` task rather than the `test` task of every project that depends on it. Tasks that read most of a project, like `lint`, narrow very little.

Task selection can also pick up a task that project selection misses. A `dependsOn` that names another project's target, like `{ "projects": ["lib"], "target": "build" }`, adds an edge the project graph doesn't record. When the task reads that target's output through `dependentTasksOutputFiles`, task selection follows the edge and project selection can't.

-Set the variable for the whole CI job, so `nx show projects --affected -t test` and `nx affected -t test` in the same script see the same affected set. The run also executes the tasks the affected ones depend on, and those can restore from cache when nothing in them changed.
+The run also executes the tasks the affected ones depend on, and those can restore from cache when nothing in them changed.
+To select whole projects instead, so every task of every affected project runs, set `affected.legacy` to `true` in `nx.json`:
+Running `nx migrate` to Nx 24 writes this setting into existing workspaces, so upgrading doesn't change what runs. Remove it, or set it to `false`, to select tasks.

+`NX_LEGACY_AFFECTED` overrides the setting for one invocation. `true` selects projects and `false` selects tasks. Set it for the whole CI job, so `nx show projects --affected -t test` and `nx affected -t test` in the same script see the same affected set.
+The setting applies to `nx affected -t` and `nx show projects --affected -t`. `nx graph --affected` always shows projects.
-{% aside type="caution" title="What changes when you opt in" %}
+{% aside type="caution" title="What task selection changes" %}
Nx selects a task when your change reaches one of its inputs, rather than by where the task sits in the task graph.

**`dependsOn` alone doesn't make a task affected.** A change to a dependency reaches a task only through the task's own inputs, for example `^production` or the dependency's build output through [`dependentTasksOutputFiles`](/docs/reference/inputs#outputs-of-dependent-tasks). An edge that only orders the two tasks doesn't carry the change across.

+The `affected` block configures how `nx affected` selects what to run.
+By default, only tasks whose inputs a change reaches run. Set `legacy` to `true` to run every task of every affected project instead:
+`legacy` applies to `nx affected -t` and `nx show projects --affected -t`. The [`NX_LEGACY_AFFECTED`](/docs/reference/environment-variables) environment variable overrides it for one invocation.
+`affected.defaultBase` is deprecated. Use the top-level [`defaultBase`](#default-base) instead.
+For how the affected set is computed, see [run only tasks affected by a PR](/docs/features/ci-features/affected).

Target defaults provide a way to configure common options for targets across projects without duplicating the configuration. When Nx builds a project's configuration, it applies applicable defaults for each target as the base for that target's configuration.
